earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog shows only Ross 2014 classification; no grammar/phonology of Mutu (Tuam-Mutu) located.

sources.citation: Bugenhagen, Robert D. 2010. Event integrity and continuity in the Tuam language. In Bowden, Himmelmann & Ross (eds), A journey through Austronesian and Papuan linguistic and cultural space: papers in honour of Andrew K. Pawley (Pacific Linguistics 615), 455-474. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026.J68 2010); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .J68 2010
sources.note: Silent on stress. Only phonological remark is the orthography footnote on p. 455: 'In the orthography, nearly all symbols have their normal phonetic values. Gh represents a voiced velar fricative, v a bilabial fricative, and doubled vowels (aa, ee, ii, oo, uu) represent long vowels.' Also states that Saveeng has three dialects: Tuam, Oov ('Mutu'), and Malai.

sources.citation: Bugenhagen, Salme E. 2009. Saveeng organised phonology data. 14 pp. Draft manuscript. SIL Language & Culture Archives, entry 31036.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: An SIL-PNG Organised Phonology Data sheet for the language (subject language Mutu [tuc]); OPDs follow a fixed template that includes a suprasegmentals/stress section, so this is the most likely place for an explicit statement of Tuam/Mutu stress placement. Listed as available online but the PDF is could not be reached by automated download; someone opening it in an ordinary browser should get it in seconds.
